==============================================================================UBiQTree R Demonstration Experiment & Automated Report GeneratorModeled on Dubey et al., Patterns 7, 101454 (2026) — MIMIC-III LOS CohortGenerates:1. Clinical_LOS_UBiQTree_Report.docx (Microsoft Word Report)2. Clinical_LOS_UBiQTree_Report.pdf  (PDF Report, if LaTeX/TinyTeX installed)==============================================================================if (!requireNamespace("rmarkdown", quietly = TRUE)) {
install.packages("rmarkdown")
}
if (!requireNamespace("knitr", quietly = TRUE)) {
install.packages("knitr")
}Create the R Markdown report source filermd_path <- "demo/Clinical_LOS_UBiQTree_Report.Rmd"
dir.create("demo", showWarnings = FALSE)rmd_content <- '---
title: "Epistemic Uncertainty Quantification in Clinical Tree-Based SHAP Explanations"
subtitle: "UBiQTree Demonstration on Hospital Length-of-Stay (LOS) Classification"
date: "r format(Sys.Date(), \'%B %d, %Y\')"
output:
word_document:
toc: true
toc_depth: 2
fig_width: 8.5
fig_height: 5.5
pdf_document:
toc: true
toc_depth: 2
fig_width: 7.5
fig_height: 5.0knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  dpi = 300
)
library(LukeFrameworkR)
library(ranger)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(knitr)
1. Executive Summary & Scientific MotivationStandard Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) report single point estimates for feature attributions, masking variance caused by finite training data and ensemble tree structure randomization. Following the UBiQTree framework (Dubey et al., Patterns 2026), this report quantifies epistemic uncertainty in Random Forest feature attributions using softmax out-of-bag tree weighting and Dirichlet process hypothesis sampling.Key findings demonstrated in this clinical cohort:High Importance Does Not Guarantee Stability: Top clinical drivers (NumNotes, NumCallouts, NumTransfers) exhibit the largest mean SHAP magnitudes alongside the widest 95% credible intervals and highest epistemic standard deviations.Entanglement Between Importance and Uncertainty: Feature attribution magnitude correlates strongly with epistemic variance across ensemble hypotheses, flagging high-impact features that require domain-expert verification before clinical deployment.2. Cohort Simulation & Model TrainingWe simulate a clinical hospital Length-of-Stay (LOS) cohort ($N = 600$ patients) modeled on the MIMIC-III experimental design with three target categories: Short Stay ($< 3$ days), Medium Stay ($3\text{--}7$ days), and Long Stay ($\ge 7$ days). A stratified 70:30 train-test split is used to train a probability Random Forest classifier (num.trees = 100, probability = TRUE).set.seed(42)

n <- 600
df <- data.frame(
  NumTransfers     = rpois(n, lambda = 2.2),
  NumNotes         = round(rnorm(n, mean = 18, sd = 7)),
  NumCallouts      = rpois(n, lambda = 1.5),
  NumDiagnosis     = rpois(n, lambda = 6) + 1,
  NumProcs         = rpois(n, lambda = 3),
  Age              = round(rnorm(n, mean = 64, sd = 14)),
  NumLabs          = round(rnorm(n, mean = 45, sd = 15)),
  AdmitProcedure   = rbinom(n, 1, 0.35),
  TotalNumInteract = round(runif(n, 5, 40)),
  NoiseBiomarker   = rnorm(n)
)

latent_los <- 1.4 * df$NumTransfers +
  0.15 * df$NumNotes +
  0.9 * df$NumCallouts +
  0.25 * df$NumDiagnosis +
  rnorm(n, sd = 2.2)

df$LOS_Group <- cut(
  latent_los,
  breaks = c(-Inf, 5.2, 8.8, Inf),
  labels = c("Short_Stay", "Medium_Stay", "Long_Stay")
)

train_idx <- unlist(lapply(split(seq_len(n), df$LOS_Group), function(idx) {
  sample(idx, size = floor(0.7 * length(idx)))
}))
train_df <- df[train_idx, ]
test_df  <- df[-train_idx, ]

rf_los <- ranger(
  LOS_Group ~ .,
  data = train_df,
  num.trees = 100,
  probability = TRUE,
  seed = 42
)

pred_probs <- predict(rf_los, data = test_df[, -ncol(test_df)])$predictions
pred_class <- colnames(pred_probs)[max.col(pred_probs)]
test_acc <- mean(pred_class == test_df$LOS_Group) * 100
Training Cohort Size: r nrow(train_df) patientsHold-out Test Cohort Size: r nrow(test_df) patientsEnsemble Size: r rf_los$num.trees decision treesHold-out Test Accuracy: r sprintf("%.1f%%", test_acc)3. Epistemic Uncertainty Quantification (Medium_Stay Cohort)We initialize ubiq_explainer() with softmax temperature $\beta = 5.0$ and draw $S = 500$ Dirichlet posterior hypothesis samples ($\alpha = 0.5$) for a clinically borderline test patient in the Medium_Stay class (class_idx = 2).explainer <- ubiq_explainer(
  model   = rf_los,
  X_train = train_df[, -ncol(train_df)],
  y_train = train_df$LOS_Group,
  beta    = 5.0,
  seed    = 42
)

ambiguous_idx <- which(test_df$LOS_Group == "Medium_Stay")[1]
patient_x <- test_df[ambiguous_idx, -ncol(test_df), drop = FALSE]

res_medium <- explain_uncertainty(
  explainer = explainer,
  x         = patient_x,
  n_samples = 500,
  alpha     = 0.5,
  class_idx = 2L
)

summary_ordered <- res_medium$summary[order(-abs(res_medium$summary$mean)), ]
summary_display <- summary_ordered
summary_display$mean <- round(summary_display$mean, 3)
summary_display$std <- round(summary_display$std, 3)
summary_display$ci_low <- round(summary_display$ci_low, 3)
summary_display$ci_high <- round(summary_display$ci_high, 3)
summary_display$entropy <- round(summary_display$entropy, 3)
summary_display$sign_stability <- sprintf("%.1f%%", summary_display$sign_stability * 100)

colnames(summary_display) <- c(
  "Feature", "Mean SHAP", "Epistemic Std",
  "95% CI Low", "95% CI High", "Entropy", "Sign Stability"
)

kable(
  summary_display,
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Table 1: Epistemic SHAP Attribution Summary Ranked by Mean Absolute Impact (Medium Stay)."
)
4. Visual Uncertainty Diagnostics4.1 SHAP Summary with Epistemic Uncertainty Violins & 95% Credible IntervalsFigure 1 combines mean SHAP attribution bars with posterior violin densities and 95% credible intervals across all 500 Dirichlet sub-ensemble realizations. Wide violins indicate substantial disagreement across plausible tree subsets.plot_uncertainty_bars(
  res_medium,
  title = "SHAP Summary with Epistemic Uncertainty"
)
4.2 Posterior KDE Distributions for Top-3 Clinical DriversFigure 2 inspects the probability density, 95% credible interval shading, and directional sign stability of the top three features driving the prediction.top3_feats <- summary_ordered$feature[1:3]
kde_plots <- lapply(top3_feats, function(f) {
  plot_uncertainty_distribution(res_medium, feature = f, title = "SHAP Distribution")
})
wrap_plots(kde_plots, ncol = 3)
4.3 Multi-Metric Uncertainty Comparison (Std Dev, Entropy, Sign Stability)Figure 3 contrasts three complementary reliability dimensions across all features: attribution spread (Standard Deviation), distributional dispersion (Shannon Entropy), and directional consistency (Sign Stability).plot_uncertainty_comparison(res_medium)
4.4 Entanglement Analysis: Feature Importance vs. Epistemic UncertaintyFigure 4 evaluates the correlation between a feature's mean absolute SHAP importance and its epistemic standard deviation across posterior samples. A strong positive Pearson correlation ($\rho$) confirms that the model's most influential features are also the most sensitive to ensemble specification.ent_df <- res_medium$summary
ent_df$abs_mean <- abs(ent_df$mean)
ent_df$is_top3 <- ifelse(ent_df$feature %in% top3_feats, "Top 3 Features", "Other Features")
rho <- cor(ent_df$abs_mean, ent_df$std, method = "pearson")

ggplot(ent_df, aes(x = abs_mean, y = std, color = is_top3)) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5) +
  geom_text(
    data = subset(ent_df, is_top3 == "Top 3 Features"),
    aes(label = feature),
    vjust = -0.8, hjust = 0.5, size = 3.8, show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  annotate(
    "label", x = -Inf, y = Inf,
    label = sprintf("Pearson rho = %.2f", rho),
    hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.3, size = 4
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Top 3 Features" = "firebrick", "Other Features" = "steelblue")) +
  labs(
    title = "Entanglement: Correlation of Importance and Uncertainty (Medium Stay)",
    x = "Mean Absolute SHAP Value (Feature Importance)",
    y = "Std Dev of SHAP Value (Epistemic Uncertainty)",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
5. Clinical Deployment RecommendationsHuman-in-the-Loop Triage: Features exhibiting high epistemic uncertainty (Std > 0.15) or sign stability below 90% should trigger clinician review rather than automated clinical decision rules.Targeted Data Acquisition: High-entropy features represent prime candidates for additional clinical sample collection or feature stabilization prior to model redeployment.

)
